1	# Reading-stage guide (0_reading) — flow, constraints, and output container
2	
3	The reading stage turns each architectural drawing into a vector JSON. The model acts like an artist
4	re-tracing the original image with a set of **semantically labeled pens**, without doing any
5	spatial-topology reasoning. All topology is left to the correction stage.
6	
7	This document is the **master guide**: the error budget, the global constraints, the output
8	container (JSON format), and the processing discipline (door-healing, self-check, downstream
9	contract). Two sibling docs split off the perception and the action:
10	
11	- **How to *recognize* what each stroke is** (what walls / doors / windows / dimensions look like,
12	  across drawing styles) → [`reading_guide.md`](reading_guide.md)
13	- **What to *do* with a recognized category** (which pen / keep-or-ignore / heal) →
14	  [`pen_library.md`](pen_library.md)
15	
16	The three are wired by a shared **semantic-category vocabulary**: the reading guide outputs a
17	category label ("door", "wall", "furniture", …); the pen library maps that label to a phase-1
18	action; this guide holds the rules and the container that both feed into.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## 0. Mental model
23	
24	Think of the reading stage as "re-tracing the source image with a set of semantically labeled pens":
25	- the **wall pen** traces every stroke that drew a wall
26	- the **window pen** traces every stroke that drew a window
27	- … plus dimension chains and text annotations
28	
29	(How to recognize each element across styles → [`reading_guide.md`](reading_guide.md);
30	the pen each category maps to → [`pen_library.md`](pen_library.md).)
31	
32	**What the reading stage does**: identify which component type each stroke is, and trace its geometry by type.
33	**What the reading stage does NOT do**: merge strokes into "one exterior wall" / outline "this is a room" /
34	say "this window belongs to that wall" / judge "this wall faces outside or inside".
35	
36	All of that topology reasoning is left to the correction stage.
37	
38	### 0.1 Error budget (important)
39	
40	The reading stage and the correction stage are mutually exclusive in the kind of error each can introduce:
41	
42	| Stage | Can see | Errors it can introduce |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| the reading stage | the source image (multimodal) | **perception errors**: misread dimension, missed stroke, offset coordinate, wrong elevation x-axis direction |
45	| the correction stage | the reading stage JSON + skill rule docs + testdata_prompt metadata (**does not see the image**) | **pure reasoning errors**: wrong grouping, inside/outside misjudged, parent-child mapping wrong, IntakeOutput field wrong |
46	
47	**Implications**:
48	- **Read every coordinate as if it is final.** The default is a hard line: a position you place is
49	  taken downstream as truth — the correction stage cannot see the image to second-guess it. Once the
50	  reading stage offsets a coordinate, flips an elevation x-axis, or misreads a dimension, the
51	  correction stage takes what it gets.
52	- **The one escape hatch is the redundant channel, and it must be earned.** An offset coordinate can
53	  be recovered by correction *only if* you also emit the dimension chain that pins it in `dimensions[]`
54	  (literal `text_verbatim` + parsed `value_m`) **and** mark that stroke's `provenance` honestly as
55	  `dimension_derived`. No surviving dimension chain ⇒ no recovery. And a missed stroke, wrong
56	  category, or dimension annotation emitted as a `wall` destroys evidence outright and the redundant
57	  channel cannot save it — it must be re-read. So do not lean on "correction will fix it": either
58	  transcribe the dimension chain that backs the coordinate, or read the coordinate precisely.
59	- **Anchor against the testdata totals.** Read the building's total dimensions / floor count / floor
60	  height from `testdata_prompt.json` and use them to *check* your coordinates (the perimeter should
61	  span the stated total width/depth; per-floor z should match the floor height). This is a cross-check
62	  only — never copy testdata content into the JSON in place of reading the image.
63	- When diffing IntakeOutput, any inconsistency tied to the source image roots 100% in the reading stage; only
64	  topology / naming / field-format errors are the correction stage's.
65	- So when writing the JSON, the reading stage **prefers null over guessing** — null means "I couldn't see it",
66	  whereas a guessed value makes the correction stage treat a wrong number as truth.
67	- **Two-channel discipline**: wall/window strokes and dimension chains are independent evidence channels.
68	  A dimension annotation, cumulative tick, extension line, or window/door sub-dimension must NEVER become
69	  a `wall` stroke. Put dimensions in `dimensions[]`; put uncertainty in provenance/confidence.
70	
71	### 0.2 Effect of simulation physics
72	
73	In EnergyPlus a zone is enclosed by **surfaces (2D faces)**; a wall has no thickness concept. So:
74	- a "thick black wall" in plan is just a **centerline** (2D polyline) in simulation; the wall body
75	  width does not participate in the calculation
76	- the reading stage need not estimate wall thickness — fill `thickness_m` with `null`
77	- an elevation `wall_fill` rectangle is only a z-range signal source (which layer's z is where), it
78	  does not mean "the wall is this thick"
79	- **a door is simply ignored in energy simulation**: a "wall with a door" is, in its simulation
80	  reality, **one continuous wall**. So when the reading stage sees a door opening it heals the wall to be
81	  continuous (door-healing, see §2.1); the door symbol only triggers the heal and does not enter
82	  `strokes`
83	
84	---
85	
86	## 1. Global constraints
87	
88	- **Units**: meters, two decimals
89	- **Each image is read in its OWN local 2D frame — the reading stage does NO world placement**:
90	  - `image_kind="plan"`: x = horizontal (drawing right), y = vertical (drawing up). A plan is already
91	    drawn in plan orientation, so these read directly as the building's plan axes.
92	  - `image_kind="elevation"`: x = horizontal along that facade (purely in-image), y = height (up
93	    positive). Record WHICH facade this is and which screen direction local-x increases in the
94	    image-local `facade` block (§4); do NOT state a world axis / sign / base here — the correction
95	    stage derives world placement from the plan footprint + this facade block.
96	  - `image_kind="section"`: defined per image; record what the axes mean in `note`s, image-local only.
97	  - `image_kind="supplementary"` / `"other"`: use only when the source is not a normal plan/elevation.
98	    Keep the same image-local discipline, explain the scope/axes in notes, and do not invent topology.
99	- **Tracing rule**: write what is drawn; fill `null` when not found; never backfill defaults from
100	  background knowledge
101	- **OCR text verbatim**, do not translate
102	
103	---
104	
105	## 2. JSON Schema
106	
107	```jsonc
108	{
109	  // ===== metadata =====
110	  "image_label": "Floor 1 plan view",       // use the official label from testdata_prompt.json
111	  "image_kind": "plan | elevation | section | supplementary | other",
112	  // facade: IMAGE-LOCAL elevation orientation (elevation only; plan → null). Records which facade
113	  // this view shows and which screen direction local-x increases. NO world axis / sign / base — the
114	  // correction stage derives world placement from the plan footprint + this block (§4).
115	  "facade": {
116	    "view_facade": "South",                 // which facade this elevation shows (from the image label/metadata)
117	    "local_x_positive": "image_left_to_right", // purely in-image; NEVER "east"/"west"
118	    "mirrored": "false",                    // "true" | "false" | "unknown"
119	    "orientation_evidence": [
120	      {"source": "image_name", "detail": "label says 'South elevation'", "confidence": "high"}
121	    ]
122	  },
123	
124	  // ===== strokes =====
125	  // each stroke = one continuously drawn stroke + its semantic type (pen).
126	  // Concrete re-trace examples: the wall pen can draw a wall line from (0,0)→(15,0);
127	  // the window pen can draw an elevation/window rectangle from (1.4,1.0)→(3.8,2.8).
128	  // how to recognize each element → reading_guide.md; which pen a category maps to → pen_library.md (plan and elevation differ).
129	  // door handling: a door opening in a wall does **not** break the wall — heal the two
130	  //   segments split by the door into one continuous wall stroke, and record
131	  //   "healed door opening at <position>" in that stroke's note (in EP a wall is a continuous
132	  //   boundary face and a door is ignored, so the continuous wall is faithful to the simulation).
133	  //   A window opening is NOT healed — keep it as a window pen. Guardrails (only heal openings
134	  //   with a door symbol, do not heal a doorless open span) see §2.1.
135	  "strokes": [
136	    {
137	      "id": "S1",
138	      "pen": "wall",                        // pen type — see pen_library.md for the legal set
139	                                            // (door is never a pen: a door only triggers healing, see §2.1)
140	      "provenance": "seen",                 // seen | dimension_derived | estimated | unknown
141	      "confidence": "high",                 // high | medium | low
142	      "dimension_refs": [],                 // required when provenance="dimension_derived"
143	      "geometry": {
144	        "kind": "line",                     // line | rect | polyline
145	        "p1": [0.00, 0.00],
146	        "p2": [15.00, 0.00],
147	        "thickness_m": null                 // plan walls always null (EP zones are enclosed by surfaces, walls have no thickness)
148	      },
149	      "note": ""                            // free text, e.g. "south horizontal perimeter wall"
150	    },
151	    // rect-fill example (elevation wall body, elevation window)
152	    {
153	      "id": "S99",
154	      "pen": "window",
155	      "provenance": "seen",
156	      "confidence": "high",
157	      "dimension_refs": [],
158	      "geometry": {
159	        "kind": "rect",
160	        "x_range_m": [1.40, 3.80],          // this image's local coordinates
161	        "y_range_m": [1.00, 2.80]
162	      },
163	      "note": "south facade F2 window 1"
164	    },
165	    // polyline example (non-straight wall)
166	    {
167	      "id": "S100",
168	      "pen": "wall",
169	      "provenance": "seen",
170	      "confidence": "medium",
171	      "dimension_refs": [],
172	      "geometry": {
173	        "kind": "polyline",
174	        "points": [[0,0],[5,0],[5,3],[8,3]],
175	        "thickness_m": null,
176	        "closed": false
177	      },
178	      "note": ""
179	    },
180	    // door-healing example: a door split this wall in the source; healed into one continuous wall + trace note
181	    {
182	      "id": "S101",
183	      "pen": "wall",
184	      "provenance": "seen",
185	      "confidence": "high",
186	      "dimension_refs": [],
187	      "geometry": {
188	        "kind": "line",
189	        "p1": [5.00, 0.00],
190	        "p2": [10.00, 0.00],
191	        "thickness_m": null
192	      },
193	      "note": "healed door opening at x≈7.5 (door swing seen in plan); EP wall is continuous"
194	    }
195	  ],
196	
197	  // Provenance mapping into correction's A0 evidence model:
198	  // - seen = visual existence evidence; its numeric coordinate is estimated_stroke, NOT direct_measurement
199	  // - dimension_derived = numeric transcribed_dimension and requires non-empty dimension_refs
200	  // - estimated = low-confidence estimated_stroke
201	  // - unknown or missing = legacy/unknown; correction must downgrade confidence
202	
203	  // ===== dimension chains (structured composite primitives) =====
204	  // visually a "tick + number + tick" chunk is one unit, classified on its own; the correction stage
205	  // uses it to derive coordinates. Emit the chain STRUCTURED so the closure check (Σ segments == overall)
206	  // can run and so the redundant channel (see §0.1) actually pins your coordinates. One entry per
207	  // number; group a chain with a shared chain_id; role = overall | segment | baseline; order = its
208	  // position along the chain. text_verbatim = the literal characters as drawn (truth); value_m = parsed metres.
209	  "dimensions": [
210	    {
211	      "id": "D1",
212	      "text_verbatim": "15000",             // literal OCR string exactly as drawn (truth — keep units/format)
213	      "value_m": 15.00,                     // parsed metres
214	      "from": [0.00, 0.00],
215	      "to":   [15.00, 0.00],
216	      "axis": "x",                          // x | y | z (z only on elevation)
217	      "chain_id": "C_bottom",               // groups the strings of one dimension chain
218	      "role": "overall",                    // overall | segment | baseline
219	      "order": 0,                           // position within the chain
220	      "anchor": null,                       // optional pixel bbox/anchor of the number
221	      "note": "bottom total-length chain"
222	    },
223	    {
224	      "id": "D2",
225	      "text_verbatim": "5000",
226	      "value_m": 5.00,
227	      "from": [0.00, 0.00],
228	      "to":   [5.00, 0.00],
229	      "axis": "x",
230	      "chain_id": "C_bottom",               // same chain as the overall above
231	      "role": "segment",
232	      "order": 1,
233	      "note": "segment 1 of the bottom chain"
234	    },
235	    {
236	      "id": "D3",
237	      "text_verbatim": "10000",
238	      "value_m": 10.00,
239	      "from": [5.00, 0.00],
240	      "to":   [15.00, 0.00],
241	      "axis": "x",
242	      "chain_id": "C_bottom",
243	      "role": "segment",
244	      "order": 2,
245	      "note": "segment 2; Σ segments (5+10) == overall (15) — the closure check the correction stage runs"
246	    }
247	  ],
248	
249	  // ===== text annotations =====
250	  "ocr_texts": [
251	    {"id": "T1", "text": "Office 101", "anchor": [3.00, 1.50], "note": ""}
252	  ],
253	
254	  // ===== uncaptured: seen but deliberately NOT traced into strokes (canonical TOP-LEVEL carrier) =====
255	  // Record here (top-level — NOT nested in self_check) anything "seen but not drawn into strokes":
256	  //   (1) strokes the pen dictionary can't cover (cornice / index arrow ...)
257	  //   (2) clutter actively excluded by selective extraction (furniture / paving / texture / room text boxes ...)
258	  //   (3) every healed door opening ("healed door opening at <position> on <stroke>")
259	  // "acknowledged skip" vs "silent loss" makes a world of difference at review time. A genuinely clean
260	  // drawing may be []; but if you healed a door or excluded clutter it MUST appear here (the linter
261	  // flags a healed-door note that has no matching `uncaptured` entry).
262	  "uncaptured": [
263	    "F1 plan excluded 8 furniture symbols + 2 paving fills",
264	    "healed door opening at x≈7.5 on south wall S101"
265	  ],
266	
267	  // ===== self check =====
268	  "self_check": {
269	    "all_dimensions_transcribed": true,     // are all dimension-chain numbers transcribed
270	    "all_visible_strokes_captured": true,   // did all visible strokes go into the strokes array
271	    "no_topology_inferred": true,           // did you resist grouping rooms / judging inside-outside / pairing parent-child
272	    "pens_used": ["wall"],                  // pen values actually used in this image (deduped)
273	    "unknowns_noted": [
274	      "wall thickness not dimensioned -> strokes[*].thickness_m = null"
275	    ]
276	  }
277	}
278	```
279	
280	---
281	
282	## 2.1 Door-healing guardrails
283	
284	In EP a wall is a continuous boundary face, a window is a sub-face on a wall, and a door is ignored
285	outright in energy simulation. So a "wall with a door" is, in its simulation reality, **one
286	continuous wall**. The reading stage can see the door arc / leaf at a glance; the correction stage only has coordinates and
287	cannot reliably tell apart "door / real opening / two independent walls" — so by the error-budget
288	principle, healing the door belongs to the reading stage. Effect: the correction stage always receives a clean, closed wall
289	network (one uniform, image-free, validated regime).
290	
291	**Healing ≠ assigning rooms**: the reading stage only guarantees the wall network is geometrically continuous
292	and closed; which walls enclose which room / inside vs outside / naming is still the correction stage's job
293	(§3 red line).
294	
295	Guardrails (to stop the reading stage inventing walls):
296	
297	1. **Only heal openings carrying a door symbol (door leaf / swing arc)** — the door symbol is the trigger
298	2. **Do not heal a doorless large opening / open span** — that is a real topology signal
299	   (possibly the same zone / a genuinely open boundary); welding it shut destroys information
300	   the correction stage needs. A gap alone, with no door symbol, does not count
301	3. **Do not heal windows** — keep them as a window pen (a window is a sub-face, not a boundary break)
302	4. **Always leave a trace when healing**: write `healed door opening at <position>` in that wall
303	   stroke's note, and record it in the top-level `uncaptured` list, so SVG review can verify
304	   "the heal is correct, no real opening was covered up" (the linter flags a healed-door note with
305	   no matching `uncaptured` entry)
306	
307	---
308	
309	## 3. Visual recognition vs spatial topology (the red line)
310	
311	Judging wall vs window vs wall_fill vs non-structural clutter is **visual recognition** (the strokes look different) —
312	the reading stage's domain (use [`reading_guide.md`](reading_guide.md) to recognize the element,
313	then [`pen_library.md`](pen_library.md) to map the category to a pen).
314	
315	Judging wall ext vs int / which wall a window belongs to / which walls enclose which room / which
316	floor a wall_fill maps to ←—— these are **spatial topology** judgments, all left to the correction stage.
317	
318	The reading stage must resist the second category even when it "looks obvious". The error budget only works if
319	the reading stage stays purely perceptual.
320	
321	---
322	
323	## 4. Elevation orientation (image-local)
324	
325	An elevation is read in its own image frame. Record orientation in the image-local `facade` block —
326	NOT a world-axis claim:
327	
328	- `view_facade` — which facade this view shows (North/South/East/West), from the image label/metadata.
329	- `local_x_positive` — which screen direction local-x increases (`image_left_to_right` |
330	  `image_right_to_left`); a purely in-image convention, **never** "east"/"west".
331	- `mirrored` — `true` | `false` | `unknown`.
332	- `orientation_evidence` — where the facade identity came from (`image_name` / `ocr_label` / `metadata`).
333	
334	Do **not** state which world axis the facade maps to, or its sign / base elevation — that is world
335	placement, which the correction stage derives from the plan footprint + this facade block (the
336	per-facade world-axis convention lives in 1_correction `A1 §2.2`, not here).
337	
338	Elevation window strokes use `geometry.kind="rect"` + `x_range_m` / `y_range_m` (this image's local
339	coordinates); the correction stage maps them into the world frame.
340	
341	---
342	
343	## 5. Counter-examples (recognition discipline)
344	
345	- ❌ `"pen": "wall", "is_exterior": true` —— is_exterior is the correction stage's call, do not add the field
346	- ❌ stuffing a room polygon into strokes —— a room is not a drawn stroke
347	- ❌ `"pen": "wall", "parent_window_ids": [...]` —— parent-child is the correction stage's inference
348	- ❌ splitting one continuous wall into 10 small strokes —— one stroke per continuous stroke
349	  (e.g. the south perimeter from (0,0) to (15,0) is **ONE** wall stroke, not 3; a window or door on it
350	  is a sub-face/heal, not a break)
351	- ❌ splitting a wall with a door into two wall strokes on either side —— heal it into one continuous wall + note (§2.1)
352	- ❌ welding a doorless open span into a continuous wall —— that is a real topology signal; only heal openings with a door symbol
353	- ❌ tracing a dimension-chain cumulative position or tick drawn outside the building outline as an interior `wall`
354	  —— dimension annotations are not walls; they go to `dimensions[]`
355	- ❌ turning a **window-hole edge** (the short jamb line bounding a window opening) into an interior `wall`
356	  —— the window is a sub-face, its opening edges are not partitions; over-segmentation here is the #1
357	  reading failure on cluttered plans (do not manufacture partitions from window jambs / dimension ticks / furniture)
358	- ❌ leaving the top-level `uncaptured` empty when furniture was excluded / a door was healed —— actively excluded items + heals must be acknowledged there (a clean drawing with nothing skipped may be [])
359	- ❌ `"text": "办公室"` for an image that says "Office 101" —— OCR does not translate
360	- ❌ `"thickness_m": 0.20` —— plan walls always null (simulation does not need wall thickness, see §0.2)
361	
362	(Pen-vocabulary counter-examples — wrong pen for the image kind, inventing pen values, etc. — are in
363	[`pen_library.md`](pen_library.md).)
364	
365	---
366	
367	## 6. Self-check list
368	
369	- [ ] picked the right pen dictionary by image_kind (see [`pen_library.md`](pen_library.md): plan vs elevation differ)
370	- [ ] every visible wall/window/wall_fill stroke is in the strokes array with the right pen field
371	- [ ] every wall/window/wall_fill/outline stroke carries `provenance` + `confidence`; `dimension_derived`
372	      strokes have non-empty `dimension_refs`; estimated/unknown strokes are marked honestly
373	- [ ] no dimension-chain cumulative position / tick / extension line was emitted as a wall stroke
374	      or window stroke; dimension ticks outside the building outline are not partitions
375	- [ ] elevation wall bodies split as "one wall_fill per floor" (see pen library)
376	- [ ] no rooms[] / is_exterior / parent relations or other topology fields
377	- [ ] no standalone door / stair / furniture / decoration strokes — recognized and logged (doors trigger healing), never traced as a pen (there is no `other` pen)
378	- [ ] door openings healed into continuous walls (only openings with a door symbol; doorless open spans kept), wall stroke note says `healed door opening at ...`
379	- [ ] every dimension-chain number is in the dimensions array
380	- [ ] text labels transcribed verbatim
381	- [ ] not-found fields filled with null
382	- [ ] elevation `facade` block filled image-local (view_facade + local_x_positive + mirrored); no world axis / sign here
383	- [ ] elevation outline: not drawn separately if it coincides with wall_fill edges (see pen library); confirmed for this image
384	- [ ] self_check.pens_used lists the pen set used in this image
385	- [ ] top-level `uncaptured` records everything "seen but not drawn" — out-of-dictionary strokes + actively excluded clutter + healed doors (a genuinely clean drawing may be [], but any heal / exclusion must appear)
386	
387	---
388	
389	## 7. Contract with downstream
390	
391	The correction stage receives a set of these JSONs (one per image) + testdata_prompt.json + skill rule docs, and
392	rebuilds topology:
393	- recognize closed regions enclosed by multiple wall strokes as rooms / zones
394	- judge each wall's is_exterior (whether it sits on the perimeter)
395	- map each window stroke to its parent wall
396	- translate elevation strokes into world coordinates using the image-local `facade` block + the plan
397	  footprint (the per-facade world-axis convention lives in 1_correction `A1 §2.2`), cross-check plan ↔ elevation consistency
398	- output the IntakeOutput Pydantic
399	
400	the reading stage's output is not IntakeOutput, and **should not align directly with IntakeOutput fields**.
401	the reading stage's product is just "the image, re-traced".
402

# Reading-stage guide (0_reading) — flow, constraints, and output container

The reading stage turns each architectural drawing into a vector JSON. The model acts like an artist
re-tracing the original image with a set of **semantically labeled pens**, without doing any
spatial-topology reasoning. All topology is left to the correction stage.

This document is the **master guide**: the error budget, the global constraints, the output
container (JSON format), and the processing discipline (door-healing, self-check, downstream
contract). Two sibling docs split off the perception and the action:

- **How to *recognize* what each stroke is** (what walls / doors / windows / dimensions look like,
  across drawing styles) → [`reading_guide.md`](reading_guide.md)
- **What to *do* with a recognized category** (which pen / keep-or-ignore / heal) →
  [`pen_library.md`](pen_library.md)

The three are wired by a shared **semantic-category vocabulary**: the reading guide outputs a
category label ("door", "wall", "furniture", …); the pen library maps that label to a phase-1
action; this guide holds the rules and the container that both feed into.

---

## 0. Mental model

Think of the reading stage as "re-tracing the source image with a set of semantically labeled pens":
- the **wall pen** traces every stroke that drew a wall
- the **window pen** traces every stroke that drew a window
- … plus dimension chains and text annotations

(How to recognize each element across styles → [`reading_guide.md`](reading_guide.md);
the pen each category maps to → [`pen_library.md`](pen_library.md).)

**What the reading stage does**: identify which component type each stroke is, and trace its geometry by type.
**What the reading stage does NOT do**: merge strokes into "one exterior wall" / outline "this is a room" /
say "this window belongs to that wall" / judge "this wall faces outside or inside".

All of that topology reasoning is left to the correction stage.

### 0.1 Error budget (important)

The reading stage and the correction stage are mutually exclusive in the kind of error each can introduce:

| Stage | Can see | Errors it can introduce |
|---|---|---|
| the reading stage | the source image (multimodal) | **perception errors**: misread dimension, missed stroke, offset coordinate, wrong elevation x-axis direction |
| the correction stage | the reading stage JSON + skill rule docs + testdata_prompt metadata (**does not see the image**) | **pure reasoning errors**: wrong grouping, inside/outside misjudged, parent-child mapping wrong, IntakeOutput field wrong |

**Implications**:
- **Read every coordinate as if it is final.** The default is a hard line: a position you place is
  taken downstream as truth — the correction stage cannot see the image to second-guess it. Once the
  reading stage offsets a coordinate, flips an elevation x-axis, or misreads a dimension, the
  correction stage takes what it gets.
- **The one escape hatch is the redundant channel, and it must be earned.** An offset coordinate can
  be recovered by correction *only if* you also emit the dimension chain that pins it in `dimensions[]`
  (literal `text_verbatim` + parsed `value_m`) **and** mark that stroke's `provenance` honestly as
  `dimension_derived`. No surviving dimension chain ⇒ no recovery. And a missed stroke, wrong
  category, or dimension annotation emitted as a `wall` destroys evidence outright and the redundant
  channel cannot save it — it must be re-read. So do not lean on "correction will fix it": either
  transcribe the dimension chain that backs the coordinate, or read the coordinate precisely.
- **Anchor against the testdata totals.** Read the building's total dimensions / floor count / floor
  height from `testdata_prompt.json` and use them to *check* your coordinates (the perimeter should
  span the stated total width/depth; per-floor z should match the floor height). This is a cross-check
  only — never copy testdata content into the JSON in place of reading the image.
- When diffing IntakeOutput, any inconsistency tied to the source image roots 100% in the reading stage; only
  topology / naming / field-format errors are the correction stage's.
- So when writing the JSON, the reading stage **prefers null over guessing** — null means "I couldn't see it",
  whereas a guessed value makes the correction stage treat a wrong number as truth.
- **Two-channel discipline**: wall/window strokes and dimension chains are independent evidence channels.
  A dimension annotation, cumulative tick, extension line, or window/door sub-dimension must NEVER become
  a `wall` stroke. Put dimensions in `dimensions[]`; put uncertainty in provenance/confidence.

### 0.2 Effect of simulation physics

In EnergyPlus a zone is enclosed by **surfaces (2D faces)**; a wall has no thickness concept. So:
- a "thick black wall" in plan is just a **centerline** (2D polyline) in simulation; the wall body
  width does not participate in the calculation
- the reading stage need not estimate wall thickness — fill `thickness_m` with `null`
- an elevation `wall_fill` rectangle is only a z-range signal source (which layer's z is where), it
  does not mean "the wall is this thick"
- **a door is simply ignored in energy simulation**: a "wall with a door" is, in its simulation
  reality, **one continuous wall**. So when the reading stage sees a door opening it heals the wall to be
  continuous (door-healing, see §2.1); the door symbol only triggers the heal and does not enter
  `strokes`

---

## 1. Global constraints

- **Units**: meters, two decimals
- **Each image is read in its OWN local 2D frame — the reading stage does NO world placement**:
  - `image_kind="plan"`: x = horizontal (drawing right), y = vertical (drawing up). A plan is already
    drawn in plan orientation, so these read directly as the building's plan axes.
  - `image_kind="elevation"`: x = horizontal along that facade (purely in-image), y = height (up
    positive). Record WHICH facade this is and which screen direction local-x increases in the
    image-local `facade` block (§4); do NOT state a world axis / sign / base here — the correction
    stage derives world placement from the plan footprint + this facade block.
  - `image_kind="section"`: defined per image; record what the axes mean in `note`s, image-local only.
  - `image_kind="supplementary"` / `"other"`: use only when the source is not a normal plan/elevation.
    Keep the same image-local discipline, explain the scope/axes in notes, and do not invent topology.
- **Tracing rule**: write what is drawn; fill `null` when not found; never backfill defaults from
  background knowledge
- **OCR text verbatim**, do not translate

---

## 2. JSON Schema

```jsonc
{
  // ===== metadata =====
  "image_label": "Floor 1 plan view",       // use the official label from testdata_prompt.json
  "image_kind": "plan | elevation | section | supplementary | other",
  // facade: IMAGE-LOCAL elevation orientation (elevation only; plan → null). Records which facade
  // this view shows and which screen direction local-x increases. NO world axis / sign / base — the
  // correction stage derives world placement from the plan footprint + this block (§4).
  "facade": {
    "view_facade": "South",                 // which facade this elevation shows (from the image label/metadata)
    "local_x_positive": "image_left_to_right", // purely in-image; NEVER "east"/"west"
    "mirrored": "false",                    // "true" | "false" | "unknown"
    "orientation_evidence": [
      {"source": "image_name", "detail": "label says 'South elevation'", "confidence": "high"}
    ]
  },

  // ===== strokes =====
  // each stroke = one continuously drawn stroke + its semantic type (pen).
  // Concrete re-trace examples: the wall pen can draw a wall line from (0,0)→(15,0);
  // the window pen can draw an elevation/window rectangle from (1.4,1.0)→(3.8,2.8).
  // how to recognize each element → reading_guide.md; which pen a category maps to → pen_library.md (plan and elevation differ).
  // door handling: a door opening in a wall does **not** break the wall — heal the two
  //   segments split by the door into one continuous wall stroke, and record
  //   "healed door opening at <position>" in that stroke's note (in EP a wall is a continuous
  //   boundary face and a door is ignored, so the continuous wall is faithful to the simulation).
  //   A window opening is NOT healed — keep it as a window pen. Guardrails (only heal openings
  //   with a door symbol, do not heal a doorless open span) see §2.1.
  "strokes": [
    {
      "id": "S1",
      "pen": "wall",                        // pen type — see pen_library.md for the legal set
                                            // (door is never a pen: a door only triggers healing, see §2.1)
      "provenance": "seen",                 // seen | dimension_derived | estimated | unknown
      "confidence": "high",                 // high | medium | low
      "dimension_refs": [],                 // required when provenance="dimension_derived"
      "geometry": {
        "kind": "line",                     // line | rect | polyline
        "p1": [0.00, 0.00],
        "p2": [15.00, 0.00],
        "thickness_m": null                 // plan walls always null (EP zones are enclosed by surfaces, walls have no thickness)
      },
      "note": ""                            // free text, e.g. "south horizontal perimeter wall"
    },
    // rect-fill example (elevation wall body, elevation window)
    {
      "id": "S99",
      "pen": "window",
      "provenance": "seen",
      "confidence": "high",
      "dimension_refs": [],
      "geometry": {
        "kind": "rect",
        "x_range_m": [1.40, 3.80],          // this image's local coordinates
        "y_range_m": [1.00, 2.80]
      },
      "note": "south facade F2 window 1"
    },
    // polyline example (non-straight wall)
    {
      "id": "S100",
      "pen": "wall",
      "provenance": "seen",
      "confidence": "medium",
      "dimension_refs": [],
      "geometry": {
        "kind": "polyline",
        "points": [[0,0],[5,0],[5,3],[8,3]],
        "thickness_m": null,
        "closed": false
      },
      "note": ""
    },
    // door-healing example: a door split this wall in the source; healed into one continuous wall + trace note
    {
      "id": "S101",
      "pen": "wall",
      "provenance": "seen",
      "confidence": "high",
      "dimension_refs": [],
      "geometry": {
        "kind": "line",
        "p1": [5.00, 0.00],
        "p2": [10.00, 0.00],
        "thickness_m": null
      },
      "note": "healed door opening at x≈7.5 (door swing seen in plan); EP wall is continuous"
    }
  ],

  // Provenance mapping into correction's A0 evidence model:
  // - seen = visual existence evidence; its numeric coordinate is estimated_stroke, NOT direct_measurement
  // - dimension_derived = numeric transcribed_dimension and requires non-empty dimension_refs
  // - estimated = low-confidence estimated_stroke
  // - unknown or missing = legacy/unknown; correction must downgrade confidence

  // ===== dimension chains (structured composite primitives) =====
  // visually a "tick + number + tick" chunk is one unit, classified on its own; the correction stage
  // uses it to derive coordinates. Emit the chain STRUCTURED so the closure check (Σ segments == overall)
  // can run and so the redundant channel (see §0.1) actually pins your coordinates. One entry per
  // number; group a chain with a shared chain_id; role = overall | segment | baseline; order = its
  // position along the chain. text_verbatim = the literal characters as drawn (truth); value_m = parsed metres.
  "dimensions": [
    {
      "id": "D1",
      "text_verbatim": "15000",             // literal OCR string exactly as drawn (truth — keep units/format)
      "value_m": 15.00,                     // parsed metres
      "from": [0.00, 0.00],
      "to":   [15.00, 0.00],
      "axis": "x",                          // x | y | z (z only on elevation)
      "chain_id": "C_bottom",               // groups the strings of one dimension chain
      "role": "overall",                    // overall | segment | baseline
      "order": 0,                           // position within the chain
      "anchor": null,                       // optional pixel bbox/anchor of the number
      "note": "bottom total-length chain"
    },
    {
      "id": "D2",
      "text_verbatim": "5000",
      "value_m": 5.00,
      "from": [0.00, 0.00],
      "to":   [5.00, 0.00],
      "axis": "x",
      "chain_id": "C_bottom",               // same chain as the overall above
      "role": "segment",
      "order": 1,
      "note": "segment 1 of the bottom chain"
    },
    {
      "id": "D3",
      "text_verbatim": "10000",
      "value_m": 10.00,
      "from": [5.00, 0.00],
      "to":   [15.00, 0.00],
      "axis": "x",
      "chain_id": "C_bottom",
      "role": "segment",
      "order": 2,
      "note": "segment 2; Σ segments (5+10) == overall (15) — the closure check the correction stage runs"
    }
  ],

  // ===== text annotations =====
  "ocr_texts": [
    {"id": "T1", "text": "Office 101", "anchor": [3.00, 1.50], "note": ""}
  ],

  // ===== uncaptured: seen but deliberately NOT traced into strokes (canonical TOP-LEVEL carrier) =====
  // Record here (top-level — NOT nested in self_check) anything "seen but not drawn into strokes":
  //   (1) strokes the pen dictionary can't cover (cornice / index arrow ...)
  //   (2) clutter actively excluded by selective extraction (furniture / paving / texture / room text boxes ...)
  //   (3) every healed door opening ("healed door opening at <position> on <stroke>")
  // "acknowledged skip" vs "silent loss" makes a world of difference at review time. A genuinely clean
  // drawing may be []; but if you healed a door or excluded clutter it MUST appear here (the linter
  // flags a healed-door note that has no matching `uncaptured` entry).
  "uncaptured": [
    "F1 plan excluded 8 furniture symbols + 2 paving fills",
    "healed door opening at x≈7.5 on south wall S101"
  ],

  // ===== self check =====
  "self_check": {
    "all_dimensions_transcribed": true,     // are all dimension-chain numbers transcribed
    "all_visible_strokes_captured": true,   // did all visible strokes go into the strokes array
    "no_topology_inferred": true,           // did you resist grouping rooms / judging inside-outside / pairing parent-child
    "pens_used": ["wall"],                  // pen values actually used in this image (deduped)
    "unknowns_noted": [
      "wall thickness not dimensioned -> strokes[*].thickness_m = null"
    ]
  }
}
```

---

## 2.1 Door-healing guardrails

In EP a wall is a continuous boundary face, a window is a sub-face on a wall, and a door is ignored
outright in energy simulation. So a "wall with a door" is, in its simulation reality, **one
continuous wall**. The reading stage can see the door arc / leaf at a glance; the correction stage only has coordinates and
cannot reliably tell apart "door / real opening / two independent walls" — so by the error-budget
principle, healing the door belongs to the reading stage. Effect: the correction stage always receives a clean, closed wall
network (one uniform, image-free, validated regime).

**Healing ≠ assigning rooms**: the reading stage only guarantees the wall network is geometrically continuous
and closed; which walls enclose which room / inside vs outside / naming is still the correction stage's job
(§3 red line).

Guardrails (to stop the reading stage inventing walls):

1. **Only heal openings carrying a door symbol (door leaf / swing arc)** — the door symbol is the trigger
2. **Do not heal a doorless large opening / open span** — that is a real topology signal
   (possibly the same zone / a genuinely open boundary); welding it shut destroys information
   the correction stage needs. A gap alone, with no door symbol, does not count
3. **Do not heal windows** — keep them as a window pen (a window is a sub-face, not a boundary break)
4. **Always leave a trace when healing**: write `healed door opening at <position>` in that wall
   stroke's note, and record it in the top-level `uncaptured` list, so SVG review can verify
   "the heal is correct, no real opening was covered up" (the linter flags a healed-door note with
   no matching `uncaptured` entry)

---

## 3. Visual recognition vs spatial topology (the red line)

Judging wall vs window vs wall_fill vs non-structural clutter is **visual recognition** (the strokes look different) —
the reading stage's domain (use [`reading_guide.md`](reading_guide.md) to recognize the element,
then [`pen_library.md`](pen_library.md) to map the category to a pen).

Judging wall ext vs int / which wall a window belongs to / which walls enclose which room / which
floor a wall_fill maps to ←—— these are **spatial topology** judgments, all left to the correction stage.

The reading stage must resist the second category even when it "looks obvious". The error budget only works if
the reading stage stays purely perceptual.

---

## 4. Elevation orientation (image-local)

An elevation is read in its own image frame. Record orientation in the image-local `facade` block —
NOT a world-axis claim:

- `view_facade` — which facade this view shows (North/South/East/West), from the image label/metadata.
- `local_x_positive` — which screen direction local-x increases (`image_left_to_right` |
  `image_right_to_left`); a purely in-image convention, **never** "east"/"west".
- `mirrored` — `true` | `false` | `unknown`.
- `orientation_evidence` — where the facade identity came from (`image_name` / `ocr_label` / `metadata`).

Do **not** state which world axis the facade maps to, or its sign / base elevation — that is world
placement, which the correction stage derives from the plan footprint + this facade block (the
per-facade world-axis convention lives in 1_correction `A1 §2.2`, not here).

Elevation window strokes use `geometry.kind="rect"` + `x_range_m` / `y_range_m` (this image's local
coordinates); the correction stage maps them into the world frame.

---

## 5. Counter-examples (recognition discipline)

- ❌ `"pen": "wall", "is_exterior": true` —— is_exterior is the correction stage's call, do not add the field
- ❌ stuffing a room polygon into strokes —— a room is not a drawn stroke
- ❌ `"pen": "wall", "parent_window_ids": [...]` —— parent-child is the correction stage's inference
- ❌ splitting one continuous wall into 10 small strokes —— one stroke per continuous stroke
  (e.g. the south perimeter from (0,0) to (15,0) is **ONE** wall stroke, not 3; a window or door on it
  is a sub-face/heal, not a break)
- ❌ splitting a wall with a door into two wall strokes on either side —— heal it into one continuous wall + note (§2.1)
- ❌ welding a doorless open span into a continuous wall —— that is a real topology signal; only heal openings with a door symbol
- ❌ tracing a dimension-chain cumulative position or tick drawn outside the building outline as an interior `wall`
  —— dimension annotations are not walls; they go to `dimensions[]`
- ❌ turning a **window-hole edge** (the short jamb line bounding a window opening) into an interior `wall`
  —— the window is a sub-face, its opening edges are not partitions; over-segmentation here is the #1
  reading failure on cluttered plans (do not manufacture partitions from window jambs / dimension ticks / furniture)
- ❌ leaving the top-level `uncaptured` empty when furniture was excluded / a door was healed —— actively excluded items + heals must be acknowledged there (a clean drawing with nothing skipped may be [])
- ❌ `"text": "办公室"` for an image that says "Office 101" —— OCR does not translate
- ❌ `"thickness_m": 0.20` —— plan walls always null (simulation does not need wall thickness, see §0.2)

(Pen-vocabulary counter-examples — wrong pen for the image kind, inventing pen values, etc. — are in
[`pen_library.md`](pen_library.md).)

---

## 6. Self-check list

- [ ] picked the right pen dictionary by image_kind (see [`pen_library.md`](pen_library.md): plan vs elevation differ)
- [ ] every visible wall/window/wall_fill stroke is in the strokes array with the right pen field
- [ ] every wall/window/wall_fill/outline stroke carries `provenance` + `confidence`; `dimension_derived`
      strokes have non-empty `dimension_refs`; estimated/unknown strokes are marked honestly
- [ ] no dimension-chain cumulative position / tick / extension line was emitted as a wall stroke
      or window stroke; dimension ticks outside the building outline are not partitions
- [ ] elevation wall bodies split as "one wall_fill per floor" (see pen library)
- [ ] no rooms[] / is_exterior / parent relations or other topology fields
- [ ] no standalone door / stair / furniture / decoration strokes — recognized and logged (doors trigger healing), never traced as a pen (there is no `other` pen)
- [ ] door openings healed into continuous walls (only openings with a door symbol; doorless open spans kept), wall stroke note says `healed door opening at ...`
- [ ] every dimension-chain number is in the dimensions array
- [ ] text labels transcribed verbatim
- [ ] not-found fields filled with null
- [ ] elevation `facade` block filled image-local (view_facade + local_x_positive + mirrored); no world axis / sign here
- [ ] elevation outline: not drawn separately if it coincides with wall_fill edges (see pen library); confirmed for this image
- [ ] self_check.pens_used lists the pen set used in this image
- [ ] top-level `uncaptured` records everything "seen but not drawn" — out-of-dictionary strokes + actively excluded clutter + healed doors (a genuinely clean drawing may be [], but any heal / exclusion must appear)

---

## 7. Contract with downstream

The correction stage receives a set of these JSONs (one per image) + testdata_prompt.json + skill rule docs, and
rebuilds topology:
- recognize closed regions enclosed by multiple wall strokes as rooms / zones
- judge each wall's is_exterior (whether it sits on the perimeter)
- map each window stroke to its parent wall
- translate elevation strokes into world coordinates using the image-local `facade` block + the plan
  footprint (the per-facade world-axis convention lives in 1_correction `A1 §2.2`), cross-check plan ↔ elevation consistency
- output the IntakeOutput Pydantic

the reading stage's output is not IntakeOutput, and **should not align directly with IntakeOutput fields**.
the reading stage's product is just "the image, re-traced".

1	# Reading-stage recognition guide (0_reading) — how to recognize what a drawing element *is*
2	
3	This is the **recognition reference** for the reading stage. It answers one question only: *given this stroke /
4	mark on the drawing, what is it?* It outputs a **semantic-category label** (`wall`, `door`,
5	`window`, `furniture`, …). It does **not** decide what to do with that label — which pen to use,
6	whether to keep or ignore, whether to heal — that is [`pen_library.md`](pen_library.md).
7	The flow, container, and discipline are in [`guide.md`](guide.md).
8	
9	```
10	this guide:        a mark  →(recognize)→  category = "door"
11	pen library:       category = "door"  →(map)→  action = "don't draw, trigger healing"
12	```
13	
14	The category label is the **handoff token** between the two docs (the vocabulary is in §0.3).
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 0. How to use this guide
19	
20	### 0.1 Recognize the stable cue, not one fixed style (important)
21	
22	Architectural drawings vary enormously — hand-drawn vs CAD, filled vs outline, schematic vs
23	construction-detail, Chinese GB / US / ISO conventions, scanned/noisy vs clean vector. **Do not
24	memorize one rendering as "the" way a thing is drawn.** For every element below, anchor on the
25	**invariant recognition cue** (the property that stays true across styles) and treat the listed
26	visual variants as *examples, not an exhaustive list*.
27	
28	- e.g. a door's invariant cue = "an opening in a wall + an indicator of how it operates (swing /
29	  slide / fold)". The swing arc, the leaf line, the sliding rectangles are all just *variants* of
30	  that indicator.
31	- When a mark roughly matches a category's invariant cue but is drawn in a style you haven't seen,
32	  **prefer the category match** over rejecting it.
33	
34	### 0.2 When unsure, recognize-enough-to-log (never silently drop)
35	
36	If a mark does not clearly fit any category, do not guess it into the wrong one. Per the error
37	budget ([`guide.md` §0.1](guide.md)), a wrong category is contamination the correction stage cannot
38	undo. Instead:
39	- give your best category guess **with low confidence in the note**, or
40	- label it `unknown` and record it in the top-level `uncaptured` list
41	
42	"Acknowledged unknown" is recoverable at review; a confident miscategorization is not.
43	
44	### 0.3 Semantic-category vocabulary (the handoff enum)
45	
46	The reading guide may distinguish finer subtypes for robustness (e.g. swing vs sliding door), but it
47	hands the pen library a **coarse category** from this fixed set:
48	
49	The second column is the **identity** (what the thing is) — the handoff label only. What to *do*
50	with each (which pen / keep / ignore / heal / route to dimensions[] / ocr_texts[]) lives entirely in
51	[`pen_library.md` §1](pen_library.md); it is deliberately not stated here.
52	
53	| category | what it is (identity) |
54	|---|---|
55	| `wall` | a room-bounding structural line |
56	| `column` | an isolated structural post |
57	| `beam` | a hidden/above-cut overhead structural line, not a room boundary |
58	| `window` | a glazed opening in a wall |
59	| `door` | a wall opening with an operating leaf |
60	| `stair` | a stepped vertical-circulation run |
61	| `vertical-circ` | an elevator / ramp / escalator |
62	| `wall_fill` | an elevation wall-body area (per floor) |
63	| `outline` | an elevation overall silhouette |
64	| `dimension-chain` | a measured span carrying a number |
65	| `level-marker` | an elevation/height value marker |
66	| `scale` | a drawing scale ratio / graphic scale bar |
67	| `grid-axis` | a structural grid line + labelled bubble |
68	| `north-arrow` | a plan orientation marker |
69	| `view-marker` | a section-cut / detail / elevation-index marker |
70	| `text-label` | drawing text (room name / note / leader) |
71	| `legend-titleblock` | a legend table / title block |
72	| `material-hatch` | a material fill pattern / poché |
73	| `furniture` | a movable furnishing |
74	| `sanitary` | a plumbing fixture (toilet / basin / tub) |
75	| `equipment` | a kitchen / mechanical fixture |
76	| `landscape-paving` | greenery / paving texture |
77	| `vehicle-figure` | a car / scale human figure |
78	| `shadow` | an elevation shading tone |
79	| `decoration` | a non-structural facade detail / attachment (moulding, cornice, band, balcony, sun-shade, railing, canopy) |
80	| `unknown` | could not classify |
81	
82	_Example image crops for the cards below are pending the v2 corpus (the `example image` field)._
83	
84	---
85	
86	## A. Drawing-type identification
87	
88	Decide *what kind of drawing* first — the element dictionaries differ by type. **Plan** and
89	**elevation** are the primary traced views. `section`, `supplementary`, and `other` are allowed
90	image kinds for ancillary sources; recognize their content image-locally and explain scope/axes in
91	notes instead of forcing them into a plan/elevation interpretation.
92	
93	- **Plan** (floor plan): a horizontal cut viewed from above (cut roughly at window height). Cues:
94	  rooms enclosed by walls, a roughly rectangular/orthogonal layout, in-plane dimension chains on the
95	  outside, room-name text inside, a north arrow, door swings. Coordinates (image-local): x =
96	  horizontal (drawing right), y = vertical (drawing up).
97	- **Elevation**: an orthographic view of one exterior face. Cues: a flat outer silhouette, floor
98	  lines stacked vertically, windows as a regular grid of rectangles, height/level markers up the
99	  side, ground line at the bottom, no room interiors. Coordinates (image-local): x = horizontal
100	  along the facade, y = height (up); orientation is image-local — see `guide.md` §4 (no world axis here).
101	- **Axonometric / perspective / 3D render**: recognize it as a **non-orthographic view** (out of
102	  scope — the reading stage only traces orthographic plans and elevations; what to do with it is the pen
103	  library's call).
104	- If a sheet has several drawings, segment by title text / frame and treat each as its own image.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## B. Line types and weights (the underlying grammar)
109	
110	Line weight and style carry meaning before you even name an element. These are *tendencies*, not
111	guarantees (many drawings have no weight differentiation at all):
112	
113	- **Heavy / thick lines** → things cut by the section plane: walls, columns. (In plan, the wall
114	  outline is usually the heaviest.)
115	- **Medium lines** → visible edges not cut (e.g. stair treads, fixtures).
116	- **Thin lines** → dimensions, extension lines, hatching, leaders, text.
117	- **Line styles**: solid = visible/cut; **dashed** = hidden or above the cut plane (e.g. an overhead
118	  beam, upper-floor outline); **dash-dot (center line)** = grid axes / centerlines; **double-dash-dot**
119	  = secondary; **freehand zig-zag / "S" break** = break line (drawing truncated here).
120	- **Color** (when present) is a weak extra cue, not reliable: e.g. blue often = glazing/water, green
121	  = landscape — but never classify on color alone.
122	
123	---
124	
125	## C. Style and medium variation (read this as a lens over every card)
126	
127	The same element looks different across:
128	
129	- **Medium**: hand-drawn (irregular lines, sketchy arcs) vs CAD vector (crisp, exact) vs scanned
130	  (speckle, broken lines, skew) vs photo of a drawing (perspective distortion, glare).
131	- **Fill convention**: outline-only (hollow double lines) vs solid poché (filled black) vs hatched
132	  (pattern fill) — all can mean the same wall.
133	- **Detail level**: schematic/diagram (single-line walls, no dimensions) vs design drawing vs
134	  full construction detail (every layer, every callout).
135	- **Standard**: Chinese GB, US (AIA), ISO — symbols for the same thing differ (e.g. dimension
136	  terminators are 45° ticks in GB/architectural practice, arrowheads in mechanical/US practice).
137	
138	Consequence for recognition: **lead with the invariant cue (what the element *does* / where it
139	sits), let visual style be secondary.** A wall is "a long boundary line bounding rooms" whether it is
140	one thick line, two thin lines, or a black bar.
141	
142	---
143	
144	## D. Structural & circulation elements
145	
146	### Card · `wall`
147	- **Appears in**: P (and E as `wall_fill`, see §E)
148	- **Stable cue**: a long, straight-ish boundary line that, together with others, encloses rooms;
149	  drawn with the heaviest weight; meets other walls at corners to close a region.
150	- **Variants (non-exhaustive)**: single thick black line · two thin parallel lines (hollow) · two lines with
151	  solid-black poché fill · two lines with hatch/material fill · schematic single line. Curved/angled
152	  walls appear as arcs/polylines.
153	- **Confusable with**: vs furniture/cabinet outline (thinner, small rectangular blocks with internal
154	  subdivision, not forming room boundaries) · vs dimension extension lines (thin, outside the plan,
155	  don't close) · vs grid axis (dash-dot, passes *through* the wall center and extends past it).
156	- **Positive test**: an interior wall bounds rooms and joins the perimeter / corridor wall network.
157	  Cumulative dimension positions or ticks outside the outline do not bound rooms and do not become walls.
158	
159	### Card · `column`
160	- **Appears in**: P (and E occasionally)
161	- **Stable cue**: an isolated small solid/filled shape (square, rectangle, circle) at a structural
162	  grid intersection, heavier than surrounding lines, repeated on a grid.
163	- **Variants**: solid black square · hatched square · circle (round column) · square with an inscribed
164	  circle.
165	- **Confusable with**: vs a wall junction (a column stands alone at a grid node) · vs furniture (column sits
166	  on grid axes and repeats regularly).
167	
168	### Card · `window`
169	- **Appears in**: P and E
170	- **Stable cue (plan)**: a break in the wall line spanned by **thin parallel line(s)** running along
171	  the wall (the glazing), with **no swing arc**. **(elevation)**: a rectangle on the facade, often in
172	  a regular repeating grid, often with internal mullion divisions.
173	- **Variants**: plan — 1 / 2 / 3 thin parallel lines (single/double/triple glazing convention) · bay
174	  window projecting outward. Elevation — plain rectangle · rectangle with mullions/grid · with an
175	  opening-direction symbol (dashed triangle) · tinted/blue fill.
176	- **Confusable with**: vs door (door has a swing arc or sliding rectangles; window has parallel glazing lines
177	  and no operation arc) · vs plain opening (opening has nothing spanning it).
178	
179	### Card · `door`
180	- **Appears in**: P (and E)
181	- **Stable cue**: an opening in a wall + an **operation indicator** (how the leaf moves). The opening
182	  + indicator together is the invariant — the indicator's exact shape varies.
183	- **Variants (non-exhaustive)**: single swing = a leaf line + a 90° arc · double swing = two leaves + two arcs ·
184	  sliding = parallel rectangles in/over the opening, no arc · folding = zig-zag leaves · revolving =
185	  circle with cross · pocket = dashed leaf into wall. In elevation: a rectangle (often floor-height),
186	  sometimes with a dashed swing-direction "V".
187	- **Confusable with**: vs window (window = parallel glazing lines, no operation arc) · vs a plain doorless
188	  opening / open span (no leaf, no arc — a real gap, **must not be treated as a door**; see the
189	  healing guardrails in [`guide.md` §2.1](guide.md)) · vs a stair/handrail arc.
190	
191	### Card · `stair`
192	- **Appears in**: P (and E/section)
193	- **Stable cue (plan)**: a run of evenly spaced **parallel lines (treads)** within a shaft, with an
194	  **up/down direction arrow** (often labeled UP / DN / 上 / 下) and frequently a diagonal **break
195	  line** cutting the run.
196	- **Variants**: straight run · L-shaped / U-shaped with a landing · spiral (treads radiating from a
197	  center) · with/without a center handrail line.
198	- **Confusable with**: vs hatching/paving (stairs have the direction arrow + are bounded by a shaft) · vs a
199	  ramp (ramp has a slope arrow + few/no treads) · **vs wall** (tread lines can resemble parallel wall
200	  lines / hatching — the direction arrow + shaft disambiguate; recognizing the stair is what keeps
201	  its treads from being traced as walls).
202	
203	### Card · `vertical-circ` (elevator / ramp / escalator)
204	- **Appears in**: P
205	- **Stable cue**: a bounded shaft with a characteristic internal symbol — elevator = box with an "X"
206	  diagonal cross and a door gap; ramp = a long strip with a slope/direction arrow and a slope ratio
207	  label; escalator = parallel treads with a long direction arrow spanning two levels.
208	- **Confusable with**: elevator-X vs a column-with-inscribed-shape (elevator is a room-sized shaft, not a
209	  point) · ramp vs stair (ramp = slope label, sparse treads).
210	
211	---
212	
213	## E. Elevation-specific elements
214	
215	An elevation carries **z (height)** information; the plan carries x/y. The two views are
216	complementary, but *combining* them (matching a plan edge to an elevation) is the correction stage's job — here,
217	just read each elevation on its own.
218	
219	### E.0 How to read an elevation (suggested order)
220	
221	1. **Outline** — the outer silhouette (top = roof/parapet, sides, bottom = ground line). Sets the
222	   overall z extent.
223	2. **Storey / floor lines** — the horizontal lines (or the level dimension chain) splitting the
224	   facade into floors. They delimit the per-floor `wall_fill` and give each floor's z band.
225	3. **Per-floor `wall_fill`** — one fill stroke per floor, bounded by those storey lines.
226	4. **Window grid + openings** — windows usually repeat as a regular grid; record each as a rect
227	   (x_range along the facade, y_range = its z band). Read each facade × floor's window chain
228	   independently; do **not** copy a "typical floor" pattern from another facade or floor. An opening
229	   that fully breaks the wall body splits that floor's `wall_fill`.
230	5. **Level / height markers** — ▽ ±0.000 etc.: the authoritative z values; transcribe verbatim.
231	6. **Attachments** (balcony / sun-shade / railing / canopy) — recognize them so they are **not
232	   mistaken for windows or storey lines**; they are non-structural (see the `decoration` card, §H).
233	
234	Stage-1 companion TODO: correction should later cross-check per-facade/per-floor window counts and
235	blank floors, but the reading stage's job is only to record each visible chain independently.
236	
237	### Card · `wall_fill`
238	- **Appears in**: E
239	- **Stable cue**: the wall-body area of the facade between two storey/floor lines — the "solid wall"
240	  as opposed to windows/openings. **Find the storey/floor lines (or the level dimension chain)
241	  first**, then read **one fill per floor** delimited by them.
242	- **Variants**: light-gray solid fill · hatched fill · or merely the area enclosed by the outline
243	  minus the openings (no explicit fill at all — infer it from outline + floor lines + openings).
244	- **Confusable with**: vs shadow (offset, one-sided, often outside the outline) · vs a material-hatch
245	  band (a material callout, not the whole wall body) · vs a decorative banding line (a `decoration`
246	  line, not a fill boundary).
247	
248	### Card · `outline`
249	- **Appears in**: E
250	- **Stable cue**: the overall heavy silhouette of the facade. Its three meaningful edges: **top**
251	  (roof / parapet / eave — sets top z), **sides**, and **bottom** (ground / grade line — the z base,
252	  usually the ±0.000 datum).
253	- **Variants**: a separate heavy frame · or simply the outer edges of the wall_fill (no separate
254	  line). Top edge varies: flat roof with a parapet (horizontal top) · pitched/sloped roof (gable
255	  triangle or slope) · stepped/setback top. Bottom may be a distinct grade line with hatching below.
256	- **Confusable with**: only record `outline` as its own element if it is drawn *separately* from the
257	  wall_fill edges; otherwise it coincides and is not a distinct stroke. A pitched roofline is part of
258	  the outline top, **not** a `decoration` line.
259	
260	---
261	
262	## F. Annotation and reference symbols
263	
264	### Card · `dimension-chain`
265	- **Appears in**: P and E
266	- **Stable cue**: a measurement line carrying a **number**, bounded by two **terminators**, with thin
267	  **extension lines** linking it back to the measured feature. The "extension–terminator–number–
268	  terminator–extension" group is one unit.
269	- **Variants**: terminators = 45° ticks (architectural/GB) or arrowheads (mechanical/US) or dots ·
270	  chained (segment dimensions in a row) vs overall (one long total) vs baseline (all from one datum) ·
271	  stacked in multiple rows (detail / axis / overall).
272	- **Confusable with**: vs grid axis (axis is dash-dot with a bubble, no number-between-ticks) · vs a leader
273	  note (leader points at one feature with text, not a measured span). Transcribe the **number
274	  verbatim**; watch units (mm vs m).
275	
276	### Card · `level-marker` (elevation / height)
277	- **Appears in**: E (and sometimes P for floor levels)
278	- **Stable cue**: a height value attached to a **filled/hollow triangle** (▽) or a level symbol,
279	  marking a z height; ±0.000 = the datum.
280	- **Variants**: triangle pointing to a line · a circle/flag with a number · relative (±0.000, 3.600) vs
281	  absolute (site elevation).
282	- **Confusable with**: vs north arrow (north arrow has an N / points up-ish, no height number) · vs a
283	  dimension number (level has the triangle/datum symbol).
284	
285	### Card · `scale`
286	- **Appears in**: P and E (usually near the title)
287	- **Stable cue**: a ratio text like `1:100` / `1:50`, or a **graphic scale bar** (a ruler with marked
288	  intervals).
289	- **Confusable with**: vs a dimension number (scale is a ratio `1:N` or a labeled bar).
290	
291	### Card · `grid-axis`
292	- **Appears in**: P (and E)
293	- **Stable cue**: a **dash-dot center line** extending beyond the building, terminating in a **bubble**
294	  (circle) containing an axis label (numbers one way, letters the other, by convention).
295	- **Confusable with**: vs a wall (axis is dash-dot, thin, runs through centers and extends past edges) · vs a
296	  dimension line (axis ends in a labeled bubble, not ticks+number).
297	
298	### Card · `north-arrow`
299	- **Appears in**: P
300	- **Stable cue**: an arrow/compass symbol marked **N / 北**, indicating plan orientation.
301	- **Variants**: simple arrow · compass rose · wind rose (combined with a wind-frequency diagram).
302	- **Confusable with**: vs a direction arrow on a stair/ramp (those sit inside a shaft and say UP/DN/slope).
303	
304	### Card · `view-marker` (section-cut / detail-callout / elevation-index)
305	- **Appears in**: P
306	- **Stable cue**: a marker pointing into a region with an **identifier** and (for sections) a **sight
307	  direction**: a cut line with flags + number, or a circle split into detail-number / sheet-number,
308	  or an elevation triangle/arrow with a label.
309	- **Confusable with**: vs grid bubble (callout references another drawing; grid labels an axis). These mark
310	  *where another drawing is taken* — **recognize so as not to mistake the cut line for geometry**;
311	  they carry no wall/window geometry themselves.
312	
313	### Card · `text-label`
314	- **Appears in**: P and E
315	- **Stable cue**: any text — room names/numbers, component annotations on **leader lines**, drawing
316	  title, general notes.
317	- **Confusable with**: distinguish a room *name* (inside a room) from a dimension *number* (on a dimension
318	  line) from a level *value* (on a triangle). Transcribe **verbatim, do not translate**.
319	
320	### Card · `legend-titleblock`
321	- **Appears in**: P and E (edges of the sheet)
322	- **Stable cue**: a bordered table — a **legend** (hatch/symbol → meaning mapping) or the **title
323	  block** (project / sheet / scale / date in the corner frame).
324	- **Confusable with**: vs a real room (title block sits in the sheet frame, contains metadata text in a
325	  grid). Use the legend to *interpret* hatches; it is not building geometry.
326	
327	---
328	
329	## G. Material and fill
330	
331	### Card · `material-hatch`
332	- **Appears in**: P and E
333	- **Stable cue**: a repeating pattern filling an area to denote a material.
334	- **Variants (per legend; non-exhaustive)**: reinforced concrete = diagonal lines + dots · brick / masonry
335	  = 45° hatch · insulation = wavy or cross-hatch · earth/compacted = specific GB symbol · sand /
336	  mortar = stipple · metal · wood (grain) · glass · water (horizontal lines). The drawing's own
337	  **legend** is the authority — read it rather than assuming.
338	- **Confusable with**: a hatch *inside the wall double-lines* = wall material (the wall itself) vs a hatch on
339	  the **floor area** = paving/finish (clutter, see §H). The location decides, not the pattern.
340	
341	---
342	
343	## H. Non-structural elements
344	
345	Recognizing these matters so they are **not mistaken for structural elements** (a furniture outline
346	read as a wall is the worst error). Identify the category honestly; what to do with each is the pen
347	library's call.
348	
349	### Card · `furniture`
350	- **Stable cue**: thin-line outlines of movable items (desks, chairs, beds, sofas), often grouped,
351	  internally subdivided, smaller than a room.
352	- **Confusable with**: built-in cabinets / bay windows can look like furniture — check whether it is flush
353	  with and continuous with the wall line (then it may be window/wall, not furniture).
354	
355	### Card · `sanitary`
356	- **Stable cue**: fixed plumbing fixture symbols — toilet, basin, bathtub, shower — standardized
357	  rounded shapes, usually against a wall in small rooms.
358	
359	### Card · `equipment`
360	- **Stable cue**: kitchen/mechanical fixture symbols (stove, sink, HVAC units, electrical symbols) —
361	  schematic icons, often with a legend entry.
362	
363	### Card · `landscape-paving`
364	- **Stable cue**: greenery (tree circles, plant symbols), paving texture (tiling grid, stippling) over
365	  outdoor/floor areas — texture covering a *region*, not a bounding line.
366	- **Confusable with**: paving texture vs material-hatch on a wall — paving fills floor area between/outside
367	  walls; wall material sits within the wall double-lines.
368	
369	### Card · `vehicle-figure`
370	- **Stable cue**: car outlines (in parking/site context) and scale human figures (for size reference).
371	
372	### Card · `shadow`
373	- **Appears in**: E
374	- **Stable cue**: a tone/fill offset to one side of the building/openings, suggesting depth/light;
375	  often gray, one-directional, may spill outside the outline.
376	- **Confusable with**: vs wall_fill (shadow is offset and directional; wall_fill sits within the facade body
377	  per floor).
378	
379	### Card · `decoration`
380	- **Appears in**: E (and P)
381	- **Stable cue**: non-structural facade lines **and attachments** — mouldings, cornices, string
382	  courses, facade banding, reveal lines, purely-cosmetic floor-divider lines; on elevations also
383	  projecting attachments: **balconies, sun-shades / louvres / fins, railings / balustrades, canopies
384	  / marquees, downpipes**.
385	- **Confusable with**:
386	  - a **floor-divider line** marking a real storey boundary is information (it delimits `wall_fill`
387	    per floor) — note it; a purely decorative band is clutter. When unsure, log it.
388	  - a **sun-shade / louvre** (slats projecting over a window) vs the **window** itself or a **storey
389	    line** — the shade projects and has repeated slats; do not merge it into the window rect.
390	  - a **balcony** vs a **floor slab** or a **window band** — a balcony projects and carries a
391	    railing; it is not a glazed opening.
392	  - a **railing / balustrade** vs **window mullions** — a railing sits at a balcony/edge, not inside
393	    a glazed rectangle.
394	
395	---
396	
397	## I. Recognition self-check (perception only)
398	
399	- [ ] decided the drawing type (plan vs elevation) before applying a dictionary
400	- [ ] for each kept mark, matched it to a category by its **invariant cue**, not one assumed style
401	- [ ] resolved the high-confusion pairs deliberately: door vs window vs plain-opening; wall vs
402	      grid-axis vs dimension-extension; stair vs paving; wall_fill vs shadow; wall-material vs floor-paving
403	- [ ] on elevations: read outline → storey lines → per-floor wall_fill → window grid → level markers;
404	      kept attachments (sun-shade / balcony / railing / canopy) out of the window/wall_fill (§E.0, §H)
405	- [ ] anything not clearly classifiable → labeled `unknown` / low-confidence note, **not** forced
406	      into a wrong category
407	- [ ] text transcribed verbatim, not translated
408	- [ ] did **not** decide actions here (which pen / keep / heal) — that is the pen library's job
409	
410	> This guide stops at *identity*. What to draw, with which pen, what to ignore, and how to heal a
411	> door — all live in [`pen_library.md`](pen_library.md) and [`guide.md`](guide.md).
